Note::is_bool¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::is_bool() const noexcept

Test The Storage Type, Not The Cell Values¶

is_bool() is true only when the receiver stores native Bool lanes. It does not ask whether text happens to contain "true" or "false", and it does not reduce a Bool Note to one truth value. Use any or all for reductions; use bools() when host code needs the lanes themselves.

Predicates and comparisons return Bool Notes, so is_bool() is also a useful contract check at the boundary between mask construction and mask consumption. Rank and shape are irrelevant: a scalar, matrix, and empty array can all be Bool. The query is constant-time, allocation-free, and noexcept; undefined returns false.

Example 1: Distinguish Bool From Text And Absence¶

const auto flags = pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false});
const auto text = pluss::note::make("alpha");
const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "flags=" << flags.is_bool()
          << " text=" << text.is_bool()
          << " absent=" << absent.is_bool() << '\n';

Output¶

flags=true text=false absent=false

Example 2: Predicate Results Are Bool Notes¶

const auto text = pluss::note::make("alpha");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "predicate=" << text.contains("a").is_bool() << '\n';

Output¶

predicate=true

Example 3: Higher Rank Remains Bool¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{true, false, false, true},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "bool=" << grid.is_bool()
          << " shape=[" << grid.size(0) << ", " << grid.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

bool=true shape=[2, 2]

See Also¶

  • Note::dtype: obtain the complete dtype enum.

  • Note::any and Note::all: reduce Bool lanes to a scalar Bool Note.

  • Note::bools(): borrow the contiguous std::uint8_t lanes.
